newsitem.title: FRANCE: India frees suspected French spies.
newsitem.headline: India frees suspected French spies.

text.p: India released three Frenchmen and a Malagasy national on Tuesday after 15 months in custody on suspicion of spying from a catamaran near a naval base, the French Foreign Ministry said.
The fate of two other French crewmembers of the catamaran "Galathee" will be decided by a court on April 2.
"Three of our compatriotes -- Thierry Proust, Herve Blanchet, Pierre-Hugues Lejeune -- and Vincent Matthew, of Madagascar, were declared free this morning," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
"They will be able to return to their families as soon as administrative procedures for their return have been completed," he added.

Indian federal police have indicted two Frenchmen -- archeologist Francois Clavel and the catamaran's captain Philippe Elle -- and two Indians for spying by allegedly carrying out illegal underwater surveys that could aid an enemy in anti-submarine warfare.
The crew members were arrested in January 1995 for allegedly carrying out an unauthorised survey of the seabed near the southern port of Cochin, site of a major Indian naval base.
An Indian businessman and a former Indian politician were also charged.

Elle has told Reuters the survey was meant to determine whether the harbour was suitable for aquaculture and could serve as a base for pleasure sailing. The "Galathee" crew was also interested in studying a 16th-century shipwreck, he said.
